chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymoun, from Humran, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) had stomach pain, so he instructed that rice be cooked for him and sumac sprinkled upon it. He ate it and was cured.
ai.seo_question: What remedy did Imam al-Sadiq use for stomach pain?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from the chain of Humran highlights the practical medical wisdom of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who prescribed rice with sumac for stomach ailments. This narration not only validates the therapeutic properties of rice in Shia tradition but also illustrates the integration of dietary remedies with spiritual authority, emphasizing that the Imams possessed knowledge of both physical and metaphysical healing.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Sa’alba Bin Maymoun, from Humran who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was with stomach pain, so he<sup>asws</sup> instructed that the rice be cooked for him<sup>asws</sup>, and the Sumac (a kind of pepper) sprinkled upon it. So he<sup>asws</sup> ate and was cured’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Faddal from Tha’labah ibn Maymun from Humran who has said the following: “
Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once experienced pain in his belly and he ordered to cook rice for him (the Imam) with sumac on it, and after eating it the pain went away from him (the Imam).’”
